text:
Sasha: Quick share from the strandbench run I kicked off this morning across us-east1 / eu-west1 on A100 / H100. Wanted a short-discussion thread on hit-rate vs p99 tradeoffs by seqlen mix. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/bench/strand/197765

Ravi: Nice — what slen mixes did you test?

Sasha: Tested three mixes: 'prod-like' (8:0.5,64:0.35,512:0.1,1024+:0.05), 'long-tail' (8:0.3,64:0.4,512:0.2,1024+:0.1), and 'short' (8:0.8,64:0.2). Each run: 5k steady-state requests, auto kernel selection, prefetch window 32, eviction LRU.

Sasha: Quick numbers (median of 3 runs) — all numbers are single-request gen p50/p95/p99 and global kv hitrate:
- A100 eu-west1 (prod-like): p50 16ms, p95 38ms, p99 89ms, hitrate 74%
- H100 eu-west1 (prod-like): p50 11ms, p95 28ms, p99 62ms, hitrate 76%
- A100 us-east1 (long-tail): p50 22ms, p95 58ms, p99 140ms, hitrate 66% (paging spikes beyond 10s for outliers)
- H100 us-east1 (long-tail): p50 15ms, p95 42ms, p99 97ms, hitrate 69%
- A100 us-east1 (short): p50 12ms, p95 24ms, p99 45ms, hitrate 88%

Jen: Those p99s are rough when seqlen > 1024 — seeing paging thrash?

Sasha: Exactly. The long-tail mix creates frequent KV evictions and re-fetches; p99 gets dominated by paging stalls and kernel re-config overhead. We saw a series of 5-20s stalls when KV store started swapping pages on the host side (trace in dashboard).

Marco: Which eviction policy did you use? LRU tends to be easy but bad for strided access. Could try LRU-2 or a tiny sampled LFU.

Sasha: LRU default for these runs. I also ran a short A/B: LRU vs sampled-LFU (sample size 64) on A100 eu-west1, prod-like: sampled-LFU improved hitrate +6pp (74 -> 80) and p99 dropped from 89ms -> 71ms. p95 improved slightly. No change to p50.

Ravi: Nice. What about prefetch window sensitivity?

Sasha: Prefetch window experiments: 8, 32, 128. For prod-like on A100 eu-west1:
- W=8: hitrate 68%, p99 118ms (too many late fetches)
- W=32: hitrate 74%, p99 89ms (baseline)
- W=128: hitrate 77%, p99 105ms (more batching helped some behind-the-scenes but latency increased due to larger scheduling windows)
So 32 looks like sweet spot for our latency SLOs.

perf-bot: nightly-strandbench artifact uploaded: s3://bench-artifacts/197765/ (contains flamegraphs + per-kernel timing csv)

Marco: Kernel choice note — auto picked GPU kernels favored "split-kv-v1" on A100 which has bad tail under heavy page-in. Forcing "fused-kv-v2" on H100 lowered kvcopy overhead. Try running with `--kernels fused_kv_v2` for long-tail.

Sasha: I did a small test: H100 + fused_kv_v2 + sampled-LFU + W=32 (prod-like) -> p99 54ms, hitrate 81%. That's the best combination so far.

Jen: Any regional capacity sizing notes? If prod traffic is long-tail, how many GPUs do we need per region to keep <100ms p99?

Sasha: Rough capacity notes based on throughput targets (peak 3k RPS sustained):
- With A100 + baseline config (LRU, W=32): you'd need ~18 GPUs in us-east1 to keep p99 ~120ms (still above target).
- With H100 + fused_kv_v2 + sampled-LFU: ~10 GPUs in us-east1 to hit p99 ~90ms at 3k RPS.
Numbers include a small safety buffer for regional variance. Details and math in artifact/summary.

Ravi: Does the model size matter here? All runs were llama-13b?

Sasha: Yes all runs used Llama-13B-ish weights quantized to q4_0 for inference. We also ran a 7B sanity check — similar trends but ~20-30% lower absolute latencies and slightly higher hitrates (smaller KV working set).

Marco: Actionable items I see:
1) Flip sampled-LFU to default for long-tail workloads behind a feature flag.
2) Add kernel override to rollout plan (fused_kv_v2 for H100-heavy fleets).
3) Add pref window telemetry (W setting per request) and per-seqlen hitrate curve to console.
4) Re-run strandbench with LRU-2 and different sample sizes for LFU, capture host paging counters.

Jen: +1 on telemetry. Also we should add a regression test that fails CI if p99 increases >10% vs baseline for the prod-like mix.

ci-bot: Regression job queued: regression/kv-strandbench/197765. Will run against baseline SHA ab12c3.

Sasha: I'll carve out time to run the follow-ups and open a PR for the sampled-LFU flag. Putting a short doc in the repo with the exact commands I used: 
```bash
# example run
./bin/strandbench --model llama-13b --quant q4_0 --kernels auto --region eu-west1 --gpus a100 --slen-mix "8:0.5,64:0.35,512:0.1,1024:0.05" --prefetch 32 --evict sampled-lfu --lfu-sample 64 --out s3://bench-artifacts/197765
```

Ravi: Thanks Sasha. Once the CFD runs are in we'll pick defaults. Can you drop the perf CSV into the eng-ml channel when ready?

Sasha: Yep — will post CSV + heatmaps later today. TL;DR: H100 + fused_kv_v2 + sampled-LFU + W=32 looks like the best path to balance cost/latency for long-tail mixes.

Marco: Good stuff. Thanks for running this.

Sasha: Thanks all :tada:
